claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or an equivalent derivative has room-temperature coercivity of approximately 100 Oe or less.
Aging at approximately 500–600°C for 2–8 hours followed by rapid quenching can induce nanoscale L1₀-type precipitates in an fcc FeCoNi-based alloy.
The aging treatment can produce coherent ordered precipitates without extensive grain growth.
The aged material will retain a predominantly fcc matrix containing a minor volume fraction of nanoscale L1₀ precipitates.
Nanoscale coherent L1₀-type precipitates act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning by the precipitates hinders domain-wall motion during magnetic-field reversal.
Hindered domain-wall motion increases the energy barrier for magnetization switching.
The increased switching barrier raises coercivity.
The aged alloy will exhibit room-temperature coercivity significantly above the approximately 100 Oe baseline.
The aged alloy will maintain high saturation magnetization while its coercivity increases.
The coercivity increase will depend on aging temperature, aging duration, and the resulting precipitate volume fraction and distribution.
